_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, moat and critiques for Syngene International, using only material published on or before 30-Sep-2026. Later facts sit in updates/later-facts.json.

industry.marketsSrc: Frost & Sullivan via Syngene AR FY26 MD&A pp.182-186 (US$ bn)
industry.drivers: Pharma patent cliff 2024-28 and US drug-price pressure (IRA) push cost-cutting and outsourcing; biotech funding recovered in H2-2025 but reaches CRO revenue with a 6-12 month lag; new modalities (ADCs, peptides, oligonucleotides, bispecifics) are over 40% of clinical pipelines (q4call); China+1 pilots and vendor qualification; AI may shorten individual programmes but widen the pool of candidates (AR26 MD&A).
industry.biosecure: The BIOSECURE Act became US law in Dec-2025 inside the defence authorisation act. The final text names no company: it relies on the Defense Department's 1260H list and a later list of 'biotechnology companies of concern', with due process and grandfathering of existing contracts, so the near-term effect is gradual (AR26 MD&A p.183). Syngene says enquiry levels and RFPs for non-China CRDMOs have risen (AR26) and that the listing of some Chinese companies helps shift molecules to India (CEO, q1call). In FY26 the Act's delays also held back client spending on research projects (AR26 p.185). We see no sign of it in Syngene's revenue yet: Q1FY27 revenue fell 16%.
industry.tariffs: Management assesses the impact of US Section 232 pharma tariffs on Syngene as negligible; RFPs continue (q4call). The US Bayview site is pitched to clients who want US-made biologics (q1call).

street.note: Latest note found for each broker, standing on 30-Sep-2026. Methods are rarely visible in accessible material. The brokers that disclose a method for Syngene use EV/EBITDA: ICICI Securities (24x FY27E EBITDA in its last accessible note, Apr-2025; its Jul-2026 view is known only from a Reuters summary), Kotak Securities' retail desk (EV/EBITDA table, older) and Nuvama, which values Syngene inside its Biocon sum of the parts at 22x EV/EBITDA (Nov-2025). YES Securities' Nov-2025 note shows EV/EBITDA in its valuation table (25.0x FY26E, 19.1x FY27E) but the basis of its Jan-2026 Sell target was not accessible. Jefferies, Macquarie, Goldman Sachs and Kotak Institutional targets come from news and tracker pages without a method. No broker in accessible material used P/E as the stated basis. Consensus (LSEG, 30-Jul-2026, after Q1): eight brokerages, average rating Buy, median target Rs532.

moat.factor: Scale and breadth (discovery to commercial, small and large molecules)
moat.why: One of India's largest integrated CRDMOs: 5,778 scientists, ~3 mn sq ft, biologics manufacturing that few Indian peers have
BMS since 1998, extended to 2035; the Zoetis commercial supply that was meant to anchor biologics manufacturing has largely gone
Management itself says Syngene drifted into commoditised research services where it loses clients to cheaper rivals (q1call)
USFDA, EMA, PMDA, UK VMD approvals; 85 audits in FY26; 6 successful USFDA audits in five years
Dedicated centres and commercial supply are sticky; FTE and fee-for-service discovery is not

critiques: Bear (Jefferies Underperform, YES Sell): Librela was not a blip; research services also lost clients; guidance was cut in Jan-2026 (FY26) and again in Jul-2026 (FY27) and the stock trades at ~16x trailing EV/EBITDA, 39% below its own five-year median.

Bull (Macquarie Outperform Rs735): the CMO problem is one product; research services, biologics capacity and a new Biocon-bred management team can rebuild growth from FY28; net cash of Rs1,800 cr protects the downside.

Our view: both are partly right. The balance sheet is safe and the BMS franchise is real, but the biologics capacity (Unit 3, Bayview, the original Bengaluru plant) was built for a customer that has gone, and replacing ~$50 mn of high-margin commercial supply with clinical batches takes years, not quarters.
gaps: Revenue split by business is disclosed only as shares (FY26 ~65/35 research/CDMO; Q4FY26 59/41; Q1FY27 78/22); small vs large molecule CDMO and Librela revenue are not disclosed. Our FY26 split (Rs2,430 / 1,309 cr) and Librela estimate (~US$50 mn in FY26) are derived from management's statements.

Broker methods: only ICICI Securities (Apr-2025) discloses one in accessible material; Jefferies, Macquarie, Kotak Institutional and Goldman notes were not accessible. StreetInsider (403) and assettype/BloombergQuint (Cloudflare block) refused our tool's identity; not worked around.
No FY27 capex guidance found in the Q4FY26 or Q1FY27 materials; our Rs400-500 cr a year follows the FY26 run-rate (~US$45 mn) and Bayview operationalisation.
Bayview operating costs before capitalisation and Unit 3 utilisation are not quantified by the company.
Syngene publishes a balance sheet only half-yearly; Jun-26 net cash (Rs1,541 cr) is from the call.
conflicts: FY27 revenue guide: 'single-digit degrowth' (deck, Chairperson) vs 'mid-single-digit decline' (CFO) vs 'low single digits' (analyst paraphrase, Business Upturn). We forecast -7%.
Biocon's stake: 52.41% (Biocon Ltd, AR26 note 12) vs 52.59% promoter group (shareholding pattern, incl. Mazumdar-Shaw family). We use 52.4% for Biocon.
Stelis Unit 3 price: Rs702 cr announced (Jul-2023) vs Rs617 cr revised gross value at closing (Dec-2023); Rs395 cr paid on completion.
